result.topic_en: Opening of the paper (pp. 138–139): a general continued fraction is defined, together with its successive convergents A/𝔄, B/𝔅, C/ℭ, …, and Euler shows how each convergent arises from the previous one by replacing the last index p with p + 1/q, noting that numerator and denominator are linear in every index.

DE TRANSFORMATIONE
SERIERVM
IN FRACTIONES CONTINVAS;
VBI SIMVL HAEC THEORIA NON MEDIOCRITER AMPLIFICATVR.

§. 1.

Consideremus fractionem continuam quamcunque, quae sit
$s = a + \cfrac{1}{b + \cfrac{1}{c + \cfrac{1}{d + \text{etc.}}}}$
ac primo quaeramus fractiones simplices, quae continuo propius ad valorem ipsius $s$ accedant, quas ita formemus vt sit
$\frac{A}{\mathfrak{A}} = a;\ \frac{B}{\mathfrak{B}} = a + \frac{1}{b};\ \frac{C}{\mathfrak{C}} = a + \cfrac{1}{b + \cfrac{1}{c}};$
$\frac{D}{\mathfrak{D}} = a + \cfrac{1}{b + \cfrac{1}{c + \cfrac{1}{d + \text{etc.}}}}$
Harum igitur fractionum vltima verum valorem fractionis con-

— ) 139 ( —

continuae propositae exprimet. Hinc igitur statim patet fore
$\frac{A}{\mathfrak{A}} = \frac{a}{1},\ \frac{B}{\mathfrak{B}} = \frac{ab+1}{b},\ \frac{C}{\mathfrak{C}} = \frac{abc+a+c}{bc+1},$
Quemadmodum autem hae fractiones vlterius progrediantur sequenti modo inquiramus.

§. 2. Euidens hic est, ex fractione prima secundam oriri, si loco $a$ scribatur $a + \frac{1}{b}$; similique modo ex secunda oriri tertiam, si loco $b$ scribatur $b + \frac{1}{c}$; ex tertia vero quartam, si loco $c$ scribatur $c + \frac{1}{d}$, et ita porro. Hinc ergo, si indefinite fractio $\frac{P}{\mathfrak{P}}$ formata sit ex indicibus $a, b, c, d \ldots p$ binaeque sequentes ponantur $\frac{Q}{\mathfrak{Q}}$ et $\frac{R}{\mathfrak{R}}$, quae respondeant indicibus $a, b, c, d, \ldots q$ et $a, b, c, d, e, \ldots r$, manifestum est, ex fractione $\frac{P}{\mathfrak{P}}$ reperiri sequentem $\frac{Q}{\mathfrak{Q}}$, si loco $p$ scribatur $p + \frac{1}{q}$; ex hac vero $\frac{Q}{\mathfrak{Q}}$ oriri sequentem $\frac{R}{\mathfrak{R}}$, si loco $q$ scribatur $q + \frac{1}{r}$. Nunc vero facile patet, in fractione $\frac{P}{\mathfrak{P}}$ tam numeratorem $P$ quam denominatorem $\mathfrak{P}$ omnes litteras $a, b, c, d, \ldots p$ ita inuoluere, vt nulla earum vltra primam dimensionem exsurgat. Si enim omnes indices $a, b, c, d, e$, vt inaequales spectentur, nullius quadratum vel altior potestas vsquam occurrere poterit.
